title: Completed exchange coherence
statement:
Completed exchange of [def-weil-pbc-completed-base-change-map] is
natural in $K$, equals the identity for identity squares, and satisfies
horizontal and vertical pasting after the canonical associativity
isomorphisms.

note:
*Source note:* no Stacks Project entry states these coherence properties of
the completed exchange: Theorem 61.30.1 ([Tag
09C9](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09C9)) asserts only that the
base-change map is an isomorphism, Lemma 61.20.2 ([Tag
099N](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/099N)) gives the functoriality of
$Lf^*_{comp}$ and of $Rf_*$ alone, and the nearest recorded coherence of the
two ingredients is the commutativity of the projection formula with the base
change map, Remark 21.50.2 ([Tag
0E48](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0E48)), stated for a single
square of ringed topoi without coefficients or completion. The blueprint
adds naturality in $K$, the identity-square statement and horizontal and
vertical pasting for the completed exchange.

proof.text: The normalized ordinary coefficient cocycle and identity module direct image fix the ordinary pullback composition and identity maps and their right-adjoint conjugates.

Naturality is the naturality equation of the composite of the tower projection natural isomorphism, strict tower exchange natural transformation, and inverse direct-image/limit comparison. This works directly on the raw ambient formula, so no compatible choice of finite witnesses is needed.

The completed pullback reflection theorem makes both one-step and two-step pullback reflections of the same ordinary pullback: use the ordinary adjunction to transfer unit-precomposition bijectivity across the first pullback, with direct image preserving completeness. Extending the units in both directions gives inverse natural comparisons; unit injectivity gives uniqueness.

For the identity completed pullback, restrict to constant coefficients. The unit-normalized scalar comparison identifies its unit with the completion unit of ordinary identity pullback. Completeness makes that unit invertible, and conservative restriction reflects invertibility. The inverse unit followed by ordinary pullback identity is the required uniquely normalized comparison.

Precompose either identity-square equality with the ordinary-to-completed unit. Its injectivity on complete targets follows from pullback reflection and direct image preserving completeness. The exchange-unit equation reduces it to the ordinary identity-square equation. The completed identity unit equation and naturality cancel the remaining factors.

For horizontal pasting precompose with the unit of the outer pullback. Apply the completed composition unit equation, then ordinary-to-completed naturality and the exchange-unit equation for each inner square. Ordinary exchange naturality moves the intermediate unit to the target. The inverse completed composition unit equation cancels those units. The ordinary horizontal pasting equation is the remaining equality. All intermediate targets are complete by pullback reflection and direct image preservation.

For vertical pasting use the same injective unit precomposition. Naturality moves the ordinary direct-image composition comparison past the unit. Substitute the two exchange-unit equations, then use naturality of the target pushComp to collect its unit. The ordinary vertical pasting equation closes the result. No additional finite-origin witnesses on intermediate objects are needed.

proof_origin.place: Coherence after canonical comparisons, proved by their actual unit equations; strict-tower naturality used directly.

blueprint_sketch.statement:
The completed exchange map is natural in $K$, is the identity for identity
squares, and commutes with horizontal and vertical pasting.
blueprint_sketch.proof:
At every finite level these equations are the S0/S8 equations. They commute
with the tower transitions by naturality of coefficient reduction. Apply
$R\varprojlim$ to each equality and conjugate by the same reconstruction,
projection-formula, and direct-image/limit isomorphisms used in the definition.
The resulting equations are precisely the completed equations.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-N8-eea7a7ef5 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, the new node and every cited statement in full, plus the main-20261015 and master blueprint texts, unit sk-thm-properbasechange, and Stacks 0B54/0944/0A07/099N. Steps 1-7 hold. Base-change morphism: the definition's c^{-1}Rlim(v')s, with v'=H'R(e)H^{-1} fixed by the reviewed normalization lemma, so it does not depend on the witness. Coefficient categories: completed A_T and constant underline-A are kept distinct and compared only through Res (an equivalence on complete objects) and the comparisons chi, phi, rho, beta, delta, lambda. I recomputed the Step 3 cancellation: iota_T Res(x)=(t^0)^{-1}L(E^T)s^0 iota_S, and this equals E^c iota_S by mate-comparison (A Noetherian, P_n perfect). The mate-pasting clauses (1)-(4) match the horizontal and vertical formulas; Step 4 coherence follows from K-injective preservation, kappa normalization and the conjugate bijection; identity squares and naturality are correct. New node lem-weil-pbc-ordered-exchange-coefficient-comparison: true clause by clause. Res has an exact flat left adjoint, so it preserves K-injectives and commutes with u_*. H^a and H'^a are invertible for any morphism because (P_n)_T is perfect over A_T, so dropping properness is valid. Small cases checked: K=0, A=0, I=A, I=0 with A finite, A=Z with I=(l). It is not a restatement of the item (no identity or pasting law) and not a duplicate: lem-weil-pbc-flat-ringed-diagram-restriction gives only the termwise ingredients, and the O_E and finite-ring analogues are narrower. No cycle. Accepted tool_uses: lem-sp-completed-pullback-adjunction and lem-sp-completion-mate-comparison, both generic constant-coefficient facts with no geometric hypotheses.
